claims.text: Unprotected carbon steel or other common metallic alloys are prone to rapid chemical degradation in high-temperature molten aluminum.
A high-performance ceramic or refractory coating can protect metallic plating-equipment components from molten-aluminum corrosion and erosion.
An aluminide-based barrier layer is an example of a suitable high-performance ceramic or refractory coating.
Applying the coating will extend the service life of the equipment components.
The deposited coating forms a robust ceramic barrier layer.
The barrier layer adheres strongly to the metallic substrate.
The barrier layer prevents direct contact between molten aluminum and the base metal.
The refractory coating is chemically inert toward molten aluminum under the stated exposure conditions.
The refractory coating is mechanically resilient under prolonged molten-aluminum exposure.
Blocking direct substrate exposure inhibits corrosive reactions with molten aluminum.
The mechanically resilient barrier inhibits physical erosion of the substrate.
Coated components will degrade significantly more slowly than uncoated components.
Coated components will exhibit less surface damage than uncoated components.
Coated components will have longer service lives than uncoated components.
Uncoated metallic parts undergo rapid corrosion during continuous immersion in high-temperature molten aluminum.
Uncoated metallic parts undergo rapid erosion during continuous immersion in high-temperature molten aluminum.
Poor coating adhesion during thermal cycling may limit protection.
Mechanical stresses during operation may limit coating effectiveness.
Exposure above the coating's stability range may limit its effectiveness.
